helpful: The statpack merits table with the excluded-count guard made the baseline computation mechanical (pool 2017-2024: 359/515 = 69.7%).
CourtListener read_document on the Sixth Circuit opinion was the single most informative retrieval for a grant-moment merits cell.
The provisioned BIO full text substituted well for the unreadable petition.
gaps: A provisioned questions-presented.txt (or OCR fallback for scanned petitions) would have mattered here: the petition was fetched but carries no text layer, and the Court's QP PDF 403s on direct fetch, so the QP had to come from a secondary source.

fedcourts query has no cases-citing-authority search; the --citation filter is a known-case lookup, which made precedent retrieval (cases applying Knick/SBA List) impossible through the corpus and pushed it to the open web.

Mapping a CourtListener search cluster_id to its opinion id costs an extra get_endpoint_item round trip; read_document accepting a cluster id would save a call (and I wasted one read on the wrong id).
notes: Forward merits cell at the grant moment: no merits briefs exist yet anywhere, so the retrieval ceiling is the cert-stage record plus the opinion below regardless of tooling.
